item.question_text: An auditor is reviewing how an organization's Statement of Applicability handles the risks it has identified for its AI systems. Which description matches the coverage expected of that document?

options.text: The risks the organization has identified, together with the control measures set up to deal with them, are carried through into the document.
Only the residual risks accepted by management appear there, because treated risks are tracked solely in the risk treatment plan.
Identified risks stay in the risk register, and the document is confined to listing the controls drawn from Table A.1.
Each item of implementation guidance the organization has adopted is entered there beside the control it supports.

item.explanation: The definition of the statement of applicability (3.26, Note 2 to entry) states: "All identified risks and the risk management measures (controls) established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability."
item.key_support: All identified risks and the risk management measures (controls) established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability.

distractor_support.support: All identified risks and the risk management measures (controls) established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The coverage is not limited to residual risk; all identified risks and the controls addressing them are reflected in the statement of applicability.

distractor_support.support: Not all the control objectives and controls listed in Table A.1 are required to be used, and the organization can design and implement their own controls (see 6.1.3).
distractor_support.why_wrong: The document is not confined to Table A.1 entries, since the organization's own controls can also form part of its necessary controls.

distractor_support.support: It provides information to support the implementation of the controls listed in Table A.1 and to meet the control objective, but organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of implementation guidance in the statement of applicability (see 6.1.3).
distractor_support.why_wrong: Implementation guidance is not an item that organizations have to document or justify in the statement of applicability.

item.question_text: How does the control list in Table A.1 relate to the set of controls an organization actually operates for AI risk treatment?

options.text: Table A.1 serves as a reference set, and an organization can devise and apply controls of its own.
Annex B holds the reference controls, while Table A.1 sets out how to put each of them into practice.
Table A.1 is an exhaustive catalogue of the controls available for treating AI risks.
Controls the organization devises for itself sit outside the scope of the statement of applicability.

item.explanation: A.1 describes Table A.1 as a reference for meeting objectives and addressing risks, and adds: "Not all the control objectives and controls listed in Table A.1 are required to be used, and the organization can design and implement their own controls (see 6.1.3)."
item.key_support: Not all the control objectives and controls listed in Table A.1 are required to be used, and the organization can design and implement their own controls (see 6.1.3).

distractor_support.support: Annex B provides implementation guidance for all the controls listed in Table A.1.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The roles are reversed: Table A.1 carries the reference controls and Annex B carries the implementation guidance.

distractor_support.support: The Annex A controls are not exhaustive and additional control objectives and controls can be needed.
distractor_support.why_wrong: The Annex A list is explicitly not exhaustive, so treating it as a closed catalogue is incorrect.

distractor_support.support: The organization can provide documented justifications for excluding any control objectives in general or for specific AI systems, whether those listed in Annex A or established by the organization itself.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Controls established by the organization itself are handled in the statement of applicability alongside the Annex A ones.

item.question_text: An organization decides that eight of the controls in Table A.1 are not needed, and its Statement of Applicability simply makes no reference to them. Why is this handling of the omissions unsatisfactory?

options.text: The document is intended to record the necessary controls together with the reasoning for including or leaving out controls.
Once a control appears in Table A.1, leaving it out of the organization's control set is not an option open to the organization.
Omissions become acceptable only after the organization puts equivalent controls of its own design in their place.
The shortfall lies in Annex B, whose guidance items have to be accounted for whenever they are not followed.

item.explanation: Clause 3.26 defines the statement of applicability as "documentation of all necessary controls (3.23) and justification for inclusion or exclusion of controls", so exclusions that are simply unmentioned leave the document incomplete.
item.key_support: documentation of all necessary controls (3.23) and justification for inclusion or exclusion of controls

distractor_support.support: Not all the control objectives and controls listed in Table A.1 are required to be used, and the organization can design and implement their own controls (see 6.1.3).
distractor_support.why_wrong: Exclusion of listed controls is legitimate; what is missing here is the recorded reasoning, not permission to exclude.

distractor_support.support: Justification for exclusion can include where the controls are not deemed necessary by the risk assessment and where they are not required by (or are subject to exceptions under) applicable external requirements.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Substitution by self-designed equivalents is not the basis on which an exclusion is reasoned.

distractor_support.support: It provides information to support the implementation of the controls listed in Table A.1 and to meet the control objective, but organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of implementation guidance in the statement of applicability (see 6.1.3).
distractor_support.why_wrong: Implementation guidance is not something organizations have to document or justify in the statement of applicability.

item.question_text: An AI management system audit is being arranged, and the sponsor asks who is permitted to perform it if it is to count as an internal audit.

options.text: The organization itself, or an outside party acting on its behalf, can carry it out.
The organization's own staff carry it out; an outside party doing it makes it external.
An outside body engaged for the work turns the exercise into a third-party audit.
An audit that covers two or more disciplines at once is classed as an external audit.

item.explanation: The definition of audit in clause 3.18 states in Note 2 that "An internal audit is conducted by the organization (3.1) itself, or by an external party on its behalf." So engaging an outside party does not, by itself, change the audit from internal to external.
item.key_support: Note 2 to entry: An internal audit is conducted by the organization (3.1) itself, or by an external party on its behalf.

distractor_support.support: Note 2 to entry: An internal audit is conducted by the organization (3.1) itself, or by an external party on its behalf.
distractor_support.why_wrong: An external party acting on the organization's behalf still performs an internal (first party) audit.

distractor_support.support: Note 1 to entry: An audit can be an internal audit (first party) or an external audit (second party or third party), and it can be a combined audit (combining two or more disciplines).
distractor_support.why_wrong: Third-party status depends on the audit being external, not on whether an outside body was hired to act for the organization.

distractor_support.support: Note 1 to entry: An audit can be an internal audit (first party) or an external audit (second party or third party), and it can be a combined audit (combining two or more disciplines).
distractor_support.why_wrong: Combining disciplines describes the scope of an audit and does not make it external.

item.question_text: A data governance lead designed and runs the organization's AI risk assessment process. She is now assigned to audit that same process for the internal audit programme. Which characteristic of an audit is undermined by this assignment?

options.text: That evidence is gathered and appraised without bias by someone detached from the work.
That the programme weighs how significant the audited processes are and earlier findings.
That objectives, criteria and scope are settled for each individual audit engagement.
That the findings produced reach the managers accountable for the area examined.

item.explanation: Clause 3.18 defines an audit as a "systematic and independent process (3.8) for obtaining evidence and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which the audit criteria are fulfilled"; auditing one's own process destroys that independence and objective evaluation. The other options describe genuine programme elements that this assignment does not touch.
item.key_support: audit systematic and independent process (3.8) for obtaining evidence and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which the audit criteria are fulfilled

distractor_support.support: When establishing the internal audit programme(s), the organization shall consider the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits.
distractor_support.why_wrong: This concerns how the programme is built, not the auditor's relationship to the audited process.

distractor_support.support: a) define the audit objectives, criteria and scope for each audit;
distractor_support.why_wrong: Defining objectives, criteria and scope is unaffected by who has been selected to audit.

distractor_support.support: c) ensure that the results of audits are reported to relevant managers.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Reporting of results is a separate element and is not what the auditor's self-review compromises.

item.question_text: A support assistant released replies containing customer personal data, breaching the organization's documented handling rule. The team (i) switched the feature off, (ii) contacted the affected customers and arranged remediation, (iii) traced the fault to a redaction step missing from the text pipeline and built that check into the pipeline, and (iv) six weeks later confirmed no further leaks had occurred. Which step is the corrective action, as opposed to a correction or the handling of consequences?

options.text: Building the missing redaction check into the pipeline so the same gap cannot reappear
Switching the feature off so that no further exposed replies could be sent out
Contacting the affected customers and arranging remediation for the exposure caused
Confirming six weeks later that the fix had held and no further leaks had occurred

item.explanation: Corrective action is defined as action aimed at the cause so the failure does not come back: "corrective action action to eliminate the cause(s) of a nonconformity (3.16) and to prevent recurrence" (3.17). Only the pipeline change addresses the traced cause; the others are containment, consequence handling, and the later effectiveness review.
item.key_support: corrective action action to eliminate the cause(s) of a nonconformity (3.16) and to prevent recurrence

distractor_support.support: take action to control and correct it
distractor_support.why_wrong: Turning the feature off is the immediate correction, which leaves the underlying pipeline defect untouched.

distractor_support.support: deal with the consequences
distractor_support.why_wrong: Remediation for affected customers deals with consequences of the failure rather than its cause.

distractor_support.support: review the effectiveness of any corrective action taken
distractor_support.why_wrong: The later check is the review of whether the corrective action worked, not the action itself.

item.question_text: An AI scoring model issued incorrect eligibility decisions because a reference dataset bought from a vendor still contained withdrawn product codes. The team has already purged the stale codes from the live store. Which further step would qualify as the corrective action for this failure?

options.text: Adding acceptance checks on incoming vendor data so stale codes are caught before use
Reissuing every affected eligibility decision using the corrected set of product codes
Recording the failure and the steps taken in the organization's evidence records
Establishing whether other data feeds in use carry the same kind of defect

item.explanation: Under the definition in 3.17, corrective action is "action to eliminate the cause(s) of a nonconformity (3.16) and to prevent recurrence"; the vendor-data acceptance check attacks the cause and stops the same defect entering again. Reissuing decisions is correction, record-keeping is evidence, and looking for similar cases is part of evaluating the need for action.
item.key_support: corrective action action to eliminate the cause(s) of a nonconformity (3.16) and to prevent recurrence

distractor_support.support: take action to control and correct it
distractor_support.why_wrong: Reissuing the decisions corrects the output already produced but does not remove the cause.

distractor_support.support: Documented information shall be available as evidence of:
distractor_support.why_wrong: Keeping evidence of the failure and actions is a record-keeping duty, not the action that removes the cause.

distractor_support.support: determining if similar nonconformities exist or can potentially occur
distractor_support.why_wrong: Searching for similar cases belongs to evaluating the need for action, which precedes the action itself.

item.question_text: An AI team has documented thresholds for the quality of data used to build and run its systems. During monitoring it finds that a training set actually used in production falls below those documented thresholds. Which of the following situations, on the facts given, amounts to a nonconformity?

options.text: The training set in use falls short of the data quality thresholds the organization documented
An internal reviewer proposes a quicker labelling method that current procedures do not use
A monitored model indicator is reported in descriptive terms instead of as a number
A vendor agreement covered by the supplier process is scheduled for renewal next quarter

item.explanation: A nonconformity is "non-fulfilment of a requirement (3.14)" (3.16). The organization set and documented data quality requirements, and data actually used fails them, so a requirement is unfulfilled. The other situations describe a suggestion, a reporting format and a contract date, none of which shows a requirement unmet.

distractor_support.support: nonconformity non-fulfilment of a requirement (3.14)
distractor_support.why_wrong: An idea for a better method identifies no unfulfilled requirement, so nothing has been breached.

distractor_support.support: Note 1 to entry: Performance can relate either to quantitative or qualitative findings.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Performance findings may be qualitative, so descriptive reporting is not by itself a failure against a requirement.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall establish a process to ensure that its usage of services, products or materials provided by suppliers aligns with the organization’s approach to the responsible development and use of AI systems.
distractor_support.why_wrong: A forthcoming renewal date under the supplier process shows no requirement that has gone unmet.

item.question_text: A provider has closed out every corrective action raised in its last internal audit, verified that each one worked, and has no open findings. Regarding improvement of its AI management system, what obligation continues to apply?

options.text: It must go on improving how suitable, adequate and effective that system is
It may hold improvement work until a further finding or the next audit cycle
It limits improvement to whatever system changes the closed findings showed to be needed
It satisfies improvement by re-checking that the closed actions achieved their intended results

item.explanation: Clause 10.1 is a standing duty independent of findings: "The organization shall continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the AI management system." Waiting for the next finding, confining improvement to changes flowing from closed nonconformities, or equating improvement with effectiveness re-checks all fall short of that continuing obligation.
item.key_support: The organization shall continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the AI management system.

distractor_support.support: The organization shall continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the AI management system.
distractor_support.why_wrong: Improvement is a continuing duty, not something triggered by the arrival of the next finding.

distractor_support.support: make changes to the AI management system, if necessary
distractor_support.why_wrong: System changes following a nonconformity are one route to improvement, not the boundary of the improvement duty.

distractor_support.support: review the effectiveness of any corrective action taken
distractor_support.why_wrong: Reviewing whether corrective actions worked is a separate step from the ongoing improvement of the system.
